trace.goal: Understand the app and score a first volleyball match as a first-time signed-out visitor.
trace.persona: First-time signed-out visitor (guest), no account, arrives cold at the marketing site.
trace.journey: Reality diverges from the anchor path: there is NO onboarding/auth step on the critical path. Root "/" → AppEntryRoute → getAppEntryTarget() sends an unauthenticated guest to /marketing (MonoLanding). From there the guest goes landing → Play hub → sport-home grid → Quick setup → live scorer with ZERO auth gate. /play is a bare Route; :sport/quick is wrapped only in SportRouteGuard (validates the sport slug, not identity); the "protected scoring" logic in mobile/backButton.js is a leave-the-match confirm dialog, not a sign-in wall. The guest's match is created and saved locally (MonoQuickMatch.jsx:692 handles the !isAuthenticated branch; :716 sets sync:'idle'). So "score a first match" is genuinely friction-free and no-signup — a real strength. But the journey has holes at BOTH bookends: the HiFi-intended first-run Onboarding→Home(empty) is skipped entirely (Home first-run empty state is currentState=missing), and the match ends on a cliff because the Result/FULL TIME screen is currentState=missing — no celebratory summary, no share card, no rematch. The "understand the app" half is carried solely by the marketing landing, never reinforced in-app. Core scoring works in ~4 taps; the surrounding activation loop is unfinished.

Home first-run empty state (Band 13 HiFi) is missing — there is no in-app welcome/empty-home; the guest is dropped from marketing straight into a sport grid.
lostRisks: Redundant sport pick: the guest chooses volleyball on the landing CTA, then the Play hub shows the entire 14-sport grid again and asks them to pick + tap 'Quick'. The ?sport param only highlights, it does not skip the grid.

Setup monolith friction: the conflated 2850-line MonoQuickMatch and ambiguous format step can stall users who aren't sure which preset to choose.
Redundant re-pick + Guided orphan can shed users between the landing and the scorer before they ever score.
fixes: Ship the Result (FULL TIME) screen: final score summary + Share card + Rematch + a soft 'Sign in to save this match' — this closes the activation loop and creates the viral share hook the HiFi intends.
Deep-link the landing 'START <SPORT>' CTA straight to /<sport>/quick when a sport is already chosen, bypassing the redundant Play-hub sport grid (keep the grid only for the 'CHOOSE SPORT' path).
Fix or remove the Guided/Browse toggle: either wire 'Guided' to a real guided setup, or drop it — never route a first-timer into the orphan NewUserFlow.

Add a non-blocking 'Playing as guest — sign in to sync' chip after the first match (and optionally a first-run empty-state Home) so guest data status is visible and an account is offered without gating scoring.
Bring the sets scorer up to HiFi: add 'Tap who won the rally' coaching copy + per-set strip, and unify Undo-last-point / attribution across engines so the core scoring feels finished.
Clean up exploration debt: unify the nav label to 'Statistics' (I-066) and fix the History/Statistics loading guards (I-053) so a curious guest doesn't hit dead-feeling tabs.

critique.journey: activation — first-time signed-out guest: understand the app + score a first volleyball match. The core is genuinely strong: no-signup, local-save scoring in ~4 taps is the right call and should be protected. But the honest tap count is optimistic (landing CTA → Play-hub Quick → format select+advance → team/Start = 4–5 meaningful taps, one of which is pure redundancy), and BOTH bookends are unfinished. The scores (seamlessness 6 / intuitiveness 7) read generous: a whole redundant screen, an orphan that baits the exact persona, a missing terminal screen, and invisible guest state argue for seamlessness closer to 4–5. Not too many steps by COUNT — the problem is a removable redundant step + dead-ends, not length.

critique.transitionGuidance: Landing → Quick setup: forward push carrying sport in state; should feel like entering the app, not restarting a choice. WITHIN setup (format ↔ team): animate as internal setupStep transitions (horizontal slide + progress bar advancing), NOT route changes — and sync setupStep to history or intercept system-back to DECREMENT the step; otherwise back from the team step blows out of the entire setup and loses typed names (a real back-stack bug risk here). 'Start scoring' → live scorer is a COMMITTING transition: navigate with replace so the user can't swipe back into a torn-down setup and re-run startMatch()/create a duplicate match. Back from the scorer must fire the existing leave-match confirm (backButton.js) and resolve to a safe hub with the local match recoverable — never an orphaned matchId. Live scorer → Result: forward/celebratory, layered ABOVE the finished scorer so points can't still be tapped underneath; 'Rematch' starts fresh, system-back goes to a safe home, not back into the completed match. Guided/Browse, if kept, is an in-place mode switch — never a navigation into a separate orphan route. Global rule: no system-back from setup, scorer, or result may ever land on a broken, empty, or orphan screen.

trace.goal: Quick-score a volleyball match start to finish, then share the result or rematch
trace.persona: Casual scorer — opens the app to score a pickup volleyball match on their phone, wants zero setup friction and a fast way to share/replay at the end
trace.journey: The core loop is functionally COMPLETE today and, surprisingly, lives almost entirely inside ONE component. Only a single real route change happens (`/play` → `/:sport/quick`); everything after that — setup, live scoring, and the match-end result — is driven by internal `phase` state (`setup | scoring | result`, MonoQuickMatch.jsx:325) with no further navigation. That makes the in-match experience genuinely seamless (no route thrash, plus auto-save/resume via `se_quickmatch_draft_*`), but it also means the celebratory/terminal moments are flat inline states rather than the dedicated FULL-TIME Result, Scorecard, Share-card, or Spectator screens the HiFi reference intends (all currentState=missing). The casual scorer CAN reach their goal: score → see winner + set breakdown → Rematch or Share. But "Share" is a bare OS text handoff (buildResultShareText via navigator.share), not a graphic card or a live watch-link, and there is NO spectator/watch-live path at all — so "someone watches my match live" is a hard dead-end. The riskiest UX moment is the in-match bottom bar [Undo · Swap · Discard · Finish]: Discard destroys the match and jumps home (MonoQuickMatch.jsx:759-760) sitting one tap away from Finish, which advances to the result — an easy, unrecoverable mis-tap. Entry also has two soft forks (Browse vs Guided mode on /play; and each sport card exposing both Quick match AND Tournament) that add small decisions a "just let me play" user doesn't want.

Six action buttons (Rematch/Share/History/Stats/New Match/Home) is a lot of choice at the finish line.

trace.goal: Score a live volleyball game smoothly — including per-point attribution, undo, an in-match menu, and share-live mid-match.
trace.persona: A person scoring a live volleyball (sets) game on their phone, wanting to keep score and let friends watch.
trace.journey: The core scoring loop is genuinely strong, but the journey as defined breaks after two steps. A user lands on MonoSetsLiveScore (dispatched from :sport/quick via the 2850-line MonoQuickMatch monolith — the sets engine has no clean route of its own). Scoring is excellent: two huge tap halves ('mono-arena-half'), one tap per point, with haptic pulse (triggerHaptic(50)), a score pop animation, a serving-dot indicator, auto-save to history, and even keyboard shortcuts (Q/P/U). Undo works — a bottom-bar button plus the U key, reverting the last history entry. But three of the five anchor steps are missing in production: (1) NO per-point attribution — addPoint (line 193) just increments; the 'Tap who won the rally' / Ace-Block-Error sheet the HiFi calls for never fires (useAppScoringPrompt is wired ONLY to the exit-confirm dialog, not to scoring events). (2) NO in-match ⋯ menu (discovery currentState=missing) — functions are scattered across a cryptic top-right Side-out/Rally toggle and a flat 4-button bottom row (Undo · Swap · Discard · Finish). (3) NO share-live at all — ShareLiveMatch and convex/live.ts exist only in .claude/worktrees/wf_*, never shipped; there is no Share affordance anywhere on the scorer, and no Spectator route for a link to even resolve. So a person scoring a live game to let friends watch hits a wall: they can score and undo beautifully, then the 'attribution / menu / share-live' half of the goal is simply unreachable.

A standalone schedule/fixtures calendar is currentState=missing. The biggest structural hole is re-entry: nav tabs are Play/History/Stats with NO Tournaments tab, so resuming a running tournament forces the organiser to re-walk Play -> sport -> tournament list every time. Creation is heavy (monolith), the payoff is thin (partial standings/bracket), and re-entry is friction-heavy — so the journey completes but feels effortful and uncertain at exactly the moments that matter to an organiser.

VERDICT RATIONALE: broken, not merely shallow. The trace's own math is the tell: ~40% goal completion with THREE hard holes on the exact legs that define a "stats-minded" persona (leaderboard, player drill-down, milestones). A journey where the persona's core destinations do not exist as screens is broken for that persona, regardless of how clean the reachable 40% feels. The 4-tap / seamlessness-4 / intuitiveness-4 numbers flatter it — low tap count here reflects too FEW reachable screens, not efficiency.

STRUCTURAL DIAGNOSIS the trace under-weights: this is not a collection of bugs, it is an information-architecture failure. The records journey is forcibly split across TWO bottom-nav tabs (History = matches, Stats = team tables) plus an unlinked third area (/profile), with zero connective tissue between them. A records/stats user holds ONE mental model ("my records"); the app scatters it across three disconnected surfaces and never bridges them. That single-spine gap is the root cause; the missing leaderboard/milestones screens and the dead-end sheet are its symptoms.

The trace also over-weights cosmetic issues: I-066 (Stats vs Statistics label) and I-053 (perpetual-loading) are a rename and an implementation bug — they should not sit at the same severity as "the leaderboard does not exist." Fix them, but they are not why the journey fails.

One nuance the trace's fix gets right and should be preserved: the inline sheet (Rematch/Share/Close) is the correct pattern for QUICK ACTIONS — it is only wrong as the primary tap target for "detail."
